reading.body:
Delaware's 2025, 2026 legislative session treats data centers as a land use and energy problem, not a technology one. Two bills filed on the same day, SB312 on data centers and HB233 on large energy use facilities, address the physical footprint and the power draw as separate statutory subjects. SB353 goes further and proposes a moratorium on data center development. The state is legislating the building and the load, which is where the binding constraint on AI actually sits.

The AI-specific bills are thinner and later. HB16 amends the Artificial Intelligence Commission, HJR7 directs that commission toward a regulatory sandbox for agentic AI, and HB404 creates a schools pilot for AI and extended reality. These are institutional and educational measures. None of them governs compute, siting, or interconnection. The pattern is a state that has separated the governance of AI applications from the governance of the infrastructure AI runs on.

Privacy and data bills run alongside: HB380 on personal data, HB60 on DMV data, HB453 on surveillance-based pricing, HCR20 on student data. SCR18 creates a task force to study nuclear energy. That is the closest the list comes to generation supply, and it is a study, not a mandate.

What this data does not show is outcome. These are bill titles and dates, not enacted law, and the list carries no vote counts, committee actions, or effective dates. It also does not say how much data center capacity Delaware hosts, how much power it draws, or whether any of these measures passed. The reader should treat the volume of activity as a signal of political attention, not of settled policy.

The two data center bills filed on the same date split the problem along a jurisdictional line that matters for anyone trying to predict where a project gets stopped. SB312 amends Titles 9, 22, and 29, which are county, municipal, and state government titles, so it reaches siting and local authority. HB233 amends Title 26, the public utilities title, so it reaches the load and the ratepayer question. A developer can satisfy one and fail the other, and the two tracks move through different committees with different constituencies.

The AI bills sit in a different part of the code entirely. HB16 and HJR7 touch the Artificial Intelligence Commission, and HB404 touches Title 14, the education title. None of them amends Title 26 or the land use titles. That separation is structural rather than accidental: the state has built one channel for what AI does and another for what AI requires, and the two channels do not reference each other in any title listed here.

The appropriations and bond acts recur across both fiscal years, and they are the only bills in the list that carry money. SB335 and HB500 cover fiscal 2027, SB225 and HB275 cover the same year through different vehicles, and HB100, HB225, SB30, and SB200 cover fiscal 2026. Whatever the substantive bills authorize, the capital and operating budgets are where the state actually commits funds, and those bills are silent on data centers and AI in their titles.

What is the difference between SB312 and HB233?
SB312 amends Titles 9, 22, and 29, which cover county, municipal, and state government, so it addresses data centers as a land use and local governance question. HB233 amends Title 26, the utilities title, so it addresses them as a large energy load. Both were filed on 2026-08-25.

Did the data center moratorium pass?
The data does not say. SB353 is listed with a date of 2026-06-29 and a title proposing a moratorium on data center development, and the list contains no vote counts, committee actions, or effective dates.

Which bills actually regulate AI as a technology?
HB16 amends the Artificial Intelligence Commission, HJR7 directs that commission to work with the Secretary of State on a regulatory sandbox for agentic AI, and HB404 creates an AI and extended reality pilot in schools. All three are institutional or educational, and none amends the utilities or land use titles.

Is there any bill in the list about power generation for data centers?
SCR18 creates a task force to study nuclear energy in Delaware, dated 2025-03-25. It is a study resolution, and no other bill in the list addresses generation supply.

How many bills in the list are appropriations or bond acts?
Eight. HB100, HB225, SB30, and SB200 are appropriations or bond acts for fiscal 2026, and SB225, SB335, HB275, and HB500 are appropriations or bond acts for fiscal 2027. They are the only entries that appropriate funds.

Does the data show how much data center capacity or power Delaware has?
No. The list contains bill numbers, titles, and dates only, with no capacity figures, load figures, or facility counts.
